{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "# This workflow runs Playwright e2e tests
# For more information see: https://playwright.dev/docs/ci

name: Playwright E2E Tests

permissions:
  contents: read

on:
  push:
    branches: [ "master", "dev" ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ "master", "dev" ]

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  test:
    timeout-minutes: 60
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    strategy:
      matrix:
        node-version: [20.x]
    
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    
    - name: Use Node.js ${{ matrix.node-version }}
      uses: actions/setup-node@v3
      with:
        node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}
        cache: 'npm'
    
    - name: Install dependencies
      run: npm ci
    
    - name: Install Playwright Browsers
      run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
    
    - name: Build project
      run: npm run rollup:debug
    
    - name: Copy built files to js-dist for e2e tests
      run: cp -r js/* js-dist/
    
    - name: Run Playwright tests
      run: npm run test:e2e
    
    - name: Upload test results
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
      if: always()
      with:
        name: playwright-report
        path: playwright-report/
        retention-days: 30
    
    - name: Upload test screenshots
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
      if: failure()
      with:
        name: playwright-screenshots
        path: test-results/
        retention-days: 30",
  "rationale": "P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE applies: cancel superseded runs when a newer revision starts on the same branch or PR. Preconditions are met (runs represent the same workflow and branch/PR; a newer revision supersedes older checks). Contraindications are not met (this is a test workflow, not release/deployment work; the concurrency group keyed by github.workflow plus github.ref isolates distinct branches/PRs so they do not share a cancellation group). The change adds only a top-level concurrency block with cancel-in-progress, preserving every existing build and test step, the existing timeout, the existing npm cache, permissions, and all artifact uploads. It does not weaken permissions, add privileged actions, secrets, deployment operations, or new network access.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE"]
}
